body.statement: For every admissible radius triple for which \(\mathcal M_n\) is nonempty, the four component constructions of \texttt{def:lower-bound-handle} provide positive, class-uniform constants and four scales \(d_1,\ldots,d_4\) whose maximum is bounded below by a positive constant times \(\rho_n\).  For each nonzero component, either there are two fixed laws in \(\mathcal M_n\) with targets separated by at least \(2d_j\) and sample total variation at most \(1/4\), or there are two priors supported on fixed-sign laws in \(\mathcal M_n\) whose sample mixtures have total variation at most \(1/4\), whose target centers are separated by at least \(2d_j\), and under each prior the target lies within \(d_j/4\) of its center except with probability at most \(1/16\).
body.proof_tex:
Use the completed background, signal, companion, and completion reservoir in \texttt{def:lower-bound-handle}.  The shell-cap calculation, opposite-tilt companions, and amplitude calibration used in \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} show directly that every fixed-sign alternative obeys all member conditions of \(\mathcal M_n\), including both richness inequalities and the treatment-effect moment envelope.  The parametric distribution perturbation, the treated Gaussian tail families (including the \(\kappa=1\) multiscale family), and the empty-treated-shell coupling are fixed-law two-point experiments.  After decreasing their class-constant amplitudes, each has sample total variation at most \(1/4\) and target separation at least twice its corresponding positive scale.

For each nuisance-product channel, take the finite equal-cell refinement specified by the handle.  Its collision calculation makes the two sample mixtures have total variation at most \(1/4\) after choosing the finite cell count sufficiently large.  The sign-average identities make the mixture centers differ by twice the corresponding treated-side or control-side scale.  The displayed variance calculation for the prior target is at most a fixed multiple of its squared scale divided by the cell count; enlarging that count once more and applying the elementary second-moment bound makes the probability of a deviation larger than one quarter of the scale at most \(1/16\).  These priors are supported on the fixed-sign laws already verified to be in \(\mathcal M_n\).  The four scales are respectively the four summands of \(\rho_n\), up to calibrated positive constants.  Since the maximum of four nonnegative summands is at least one fourth of their sum, their maximum is bounded below by a positive class-uniform multiple of \(\rho_n\).
body.justification: This exported testing modulus records the fixed-law and fuzzy-prior information that the four-channel construction establishes, rather than leaving the honest-interval converse to recover it from an estimator-risk conclusion.
body.gap: A deviation lower bound alone does not supply the total-variation, prior-target concentration, or fixed-sign-membership facts needed for an honest expected-length lower bound.
body.consumer: The honest-interval theorem uses this lemma to derive its two-point and fuzzy-prior length lower bounds; the sharp-risk theorem continues to use the deviation consequence of \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse}.
